questions.prompt: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of which kingdom?
questions.fact: Her family was Greek and ruled Egypt for roughly three centuries. She was reportedly the first of them to learn Egyptian.

questions.prompt: What is the term for animals active mainly at dawn and dusk?
questions.fact: Rabbits, deer, and most domestic cats fall into this group, which is why cats often get lively around sunrise and sunset.

questions.prompt: How many strikes make an out in baseball?
questions.fact: A foul ball counts as a strike, except when it would be the third one, which is why at-bats can run remarkably long.

questions.prompt: Which video game character is a plumber created by Nintendo?
questions.fact: The moustache and cap exist for technical reasons. Early hardware could not render a mouth or hair clearly at that resolution.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest administrative capital city in the world?
questions.fact: It sits above 3,600 metres, thin enough air that visiting football teams have long complained about playing there.

questions.prompt: Which Nigerian writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986?
questions.fact: He was the first African laureate in literature, and had earlier spent two years imprisoned largely in solitary confinement.

questions.prompt: Which protocol suite underpins how data moves across the internet?
questions.fact: It breaks every message into packets that can travel separate routes and be reassembled in the right order at the other end.
